headline: Haven bid ahead of Nvidia bull-steepens Treasuries; Gulf attacks lift oil, metals steady
summary: A broad stock selloff before Nvidia's results sent money into Treasuries, pulling the 2-year down about 4bp even as retail sales beat and Fed officials stayed hawkish. WTI edged up 0.3% on fresh Gulf attacks and an expected US crude draw, but RBOB slipped to another eight-month low. Gold and silver steadied just above their one-year lows as the dollar reversed from a 19-month high, while Bunds and especially OATs rallied on the risk-off tone.
drivers: The S&P 500 fell about 1% with all sectors lower, and the 2-year dropped about 4bp to near 4.79% while the 30-year eased under 1bp to near 5.46%. A brief rise after October's retail control group rose 0.6%, about twice forecasts, quickly faded.
Gulf attacks keep a floor under crude

WTI settled up $0.29 at $86.01 and Brent up $0.70 at $93.14 after a tanker was hit twice in Hormuz, Houthi drones targeted Saudi pipeline pumps and Iran claimed a strike on a US radar in Bahrain. The IEA's fourth-quarter surplus call and Iranian talk of diplomacy capped the bounce.
Hawkish Fed talk caps the metals bounce

Musalem said several hikes may be needed and Williams called inflation stubbornly high, keeping a December hike about 98% priced. Dec gold settled 0.2% higher at $3,864.20 and Comex silver 1.1% higher at $47.29 as the dollar slipped off its high.

French 10-year yields fell about 3–5bp to near 4.88% and the OAT–Bund spread narrowed to about 153bp, despite EU forecasts showing a 5.5% French deficit this year. A strong German ZEW of 35.6 limited the Bund rally to about 1bp.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled +$0.29 (+0.3%) at $86.01 in an $84.68–87.38 range; Brent +$0.70 at $93.14.
oil.why: Crude bounced after Monday's 3% drop as a tanker in Hormuz was struck twice with its crew missing, Houthi drones targeted Saudi East-West pipeline pumping stations and Iran claimed a hit on a US radar in Bahrain, which CENTCOM denied. Analysts also expected a US crude draw this week. Gains faded late as Iranian media said Tehran was pursuing a diplomatic exit, and the IEA's fourth-quarter surplus view still caps rallies.
oil.outlook: Range of $83–90 with a mild downward bias while Gulf exports keep recovering; a close below $84 opens about $80. A real Hormuz closure or OPEC+ restraint on Nov 29 would bring $90–93 back.
oil.watch: EIA stocks Wed Nov 18, Dec WTI expiry Thu Nov 19, Gulf headlines and OPEC+ Nov 29.

gas.note: Dec RBOB slipped 0.30¢ (-0.1%) to $2.5349, a third straight drop and the lowest settle since Mar 4.
gas.why: Gasoline lagged crude's small bounce because the product side is well supplied: winter-grade blends are cheaper, autumn demand is soft and Gulf supply keeps recovering. RBOB is down about 23% this month, and AAA's national average fell to $3.78, the lowest since mid-March and about 20¢ lower in a week. Diesel also slid about 0.8%, and an Iranian diplomacy report pushed products into the red late.
gas.outlook: Bias lower in a $2.45–2.62 range while cracks stay soft; RBOB needs WTI back above $90 to break $2.65. A large EIA gasoline draw would steady it near $2.55.
gas.watch: EIA gasoline stocks Wed Nov 18, Dec contract expiry and AAA's daily average.

gold.note: Spot about flat near $3,853, off a $3,887 high; Dec futures settled +0.2% at $3,864.20.
gold.why: Gold steadied just above Monday's 13-month low of about $3,830 as Treasury yields and the dollar eased from a 19-month high late in the day. Gains were capped because Fed speakers stayed hawkish: Musalem said several hikes may be needed and Williams called inflation stubbornly high, so markets kept about 98% odds of a December 25bp hike. With 10-year yields above 5.1%, the non-yielding metal attracts only bargain buying.
gold.outlook: Bias lower in a $3,780–3,920 range while the dollar and real yields stay high; a close below $3,830 opens about $3,750. Dovish FOMC minutes or soft data would bring $3,920–4,000 back.
gold.watch: FOMC minutes Wed Nov 18, the dollar and Fed speakers.

silver.note: Comex settled +1.1% at $47.29, snapping a three-day slide; spot near $47.5 after a $46.84–48.01 range.
silver.why: Silver rebounded from a 52-week low as short-covering met bargain buying and the dollar slipped back late. It still lagged early gains because the stock selloff before Nvidia's results weighed on its industrial story and Fed hike bets stayed firm. The gold-silver ratio eased to about 81 from 82, a modest sign of stabilising.
silver.outlook: Range of $45.5–49 with a downward bias; a close below $46 opens $44–45. A relief rally in chip stocks after Nvidia's beat and a softer dollar would bring $49–50.
silver.watch: Market reaction to Nvidia's results, FOMC minutes Wed Nov 18 and the dollar.

us2y.note: Down about 4bp to near 4.79%, as the 2s10s curve steepened to about 31bp.
us2y.why: The front end rallied on a flight to quality as stocks fell more than 1% ahead of Nvidia's results and an NSA network outage added to nerves. That outweighed strong data: the retail control group rose 0.6% against about 0.3% expected, with upward revisions, and import prices beat. Hawkish remarks from Musalem and Williams did not change December pricing, where a 25bp hike stays about 98% priced.
us2y.outlook: Range of 4.72–4.90% with a neutral bias; hawkish minutes would retest 4.90%, while a deeper equity selloff could take it toward 4.72%.
us2y.watch: FOMC minutes Wed Nov 18, jobless claims Thu Nov 19 and Fed speakers.

us5y.note: Down about 2–3bp to near 4.91%, holding below last week's 4.95% area.
us5y.why: The belly followed the front end lower as haven buying before Nvidia's results outweighed a firm retail control group and hotter import prices. Five-year breakevens edged up to about 2.27%, so the drop came from real yields rather than inflation pricing. Fed speakers stuck to a tightening message but did not hint at a bigger step.
us5y.outlook: Range of 4.82–5.00% with a neutral bias; minutes that open the door to more than one hike would lift it toward 5.00%, and lower oil or weak stocks would bring 4.82%.
us5y.watch: FOMC minutes Wed Nov 18 and the 20-year auction.

us10y.note: Down about 2bp to near 5.10%, after briefly rising toward 5.14% on retail sales.
us10y.why: The 10-year rose after the retail control group came in at 0.6%, twice forecasts, then reversed as stocks slid more than 1% before Nvidia's results and haven demand returned. A plunge in homebuilder sentiment to a 14½-year low helped. The rally was smaller than at the front end because Musalem and Williams kept stressing persistent inflation, which supports term premium.
us10y.outlook: Range of 5.03–5.18% with a neutral bias; Nvidia's beat could ease the haven bid and push it back toward 5.15%. A break above 5.20% would need hawkish minutes; a renewed tech slump brings 5.03%.
us10y.watch: FOMC minutes Wed Nov 18, the 20-year auction and claims Thu Nov 19.

us30y.note: Down under 1bp to near 5.46%, lagging the curve as 2s30s steepened about 3bp.
us30y.why: The long bond barely moved because haven buying focused on shorter notes, and hawkish Fed talk plus hotter import prices kept long-run inflation worries alive. Supply concerns after last week's weak 30-year sale also persist, though Treasury's buyback of up to $6bn of long bonds gave some support.
us30y.outlook: Range of 5.40–5.55% with a mild upward bias on supply and inflation risk; a weak 20-year sale would push it toward 5.55%, while softer data would bring 5.40%.
us30y.watch: 20-year auction this week and FOMC minutes Wed Nov 18.

de2y.note: Down about 2bp to near 3.11%, ahead of a Schatz auction, off Friday's one-month high.
de2y.why: Short Bunds eased as the risk-off tone before Nvidia's results spread to Europe and Treasuries rallied. A stronger-than-expected ZEW reading of 35.6, against forecasts near 28, limited the drop. The European Commission now expects EU inflation of 3.3% this year and 3.2% next, which supports bets that the ECB hikes in December.
de2y.outlook: Range of 3.05–3.18% with a slight upward bias while a December hike is priced; weak flash PMIs or a fresh oil slide would bring 3.05%.
de2y.watch: Euro-area final October inflation Wed Nov 18, flash PMIs later this week and the ECB Dec 17.

de5y.note: Little changed near 3.18%, holding just below last week's highs.
de5y.why: The belly held steady as a haven bid during the US stock selloff offset strong German data. The ZEW expectations index jumped 7.5 points to 35.6, and the Commission raised its growth forecasts, both backing the ECB's hawkish bias. Higher energy-driven inflation forecasts kept buyers cautious.
de5y.outlook: Range of 3.10–3.25% with a neutral bias; hawkish ECB comments would test 3.25%, while weak PMIs would bring 3.10%.
de5y.watch: Euro-area flash PMIs, ECB speakers and US FOMC minutes.

de10y.note: Down about 1bp to near 3.37%, after dipping to about 3.36% intraday.
de10y.why: The benchmark eased with Treasuries as stocks fell ahead of Nvidia's results, ending a seven-day run of rises. Strong German data limited the move: the ZEW beat sharply, and the Commission lifted its growth outlook while warning that inflation will stay above 3%. Fiscal spending plans also keep term premium high.
de10y.outlook: Range of 3.30–3.45% with a mild upward bias while ECB hike bets hold; a break above 3.45% would need US 10-year yields back above 5.20%.
de10y.watch: Flash PMIs later this week, German supply and US FOMC minutes.

de30y.note: About flat near 3.74%, as the curve steepened slightly.
de30y.why: The long end lagged the small rally because heavy German borrowing plans keep investors demanding term premium, and the Commission's upbeat growth outlook rests on state spending. The risk-off tone during the US tech selloff stopped yields from rising.
de30y.outlook: Range of 3.68–3.82% with a mild upward bias; a break above 3.82% would need weak German auctions or US 30-year yields above 5.55%.
de30y.watch: German supply, the US 20-year auction and flash PMIs.

fr2y.note: Down about 2–3bp to near 3.60%, leading the short end lower.
fr2y.why: Short OATs rallied more than Schatz as risk-off flows spread from US stocks and French debt recovered some of Monday's underperformance. ECB pricing changed little, with a December hike still expected, and the Commission's higher inflation forecasts limited the move.
fr2y.outlook: Range of 3.52–3.68% with a neutral bias while hike pricing holds; a lasting oil drop that cools inflation would bring 3.52%.
fr2y.watch: Euro-area final inflation Wed Nov 18, flash PMIs and the ECB Dec 17.

fr5y.note: Down about 2–3bp to near 4.24%, outperforming Bunds.
fr5y.why: Middle OATs gained as the risk-off tone helped core bonds and investors looked past Le Pen's fiscal plans, which include lowering the retirement age for some workers. The Commission's forecast of a 5.5% French deficit this year, rising to 5.7% in 2028, was largely expected but caps the rally.
fr5y.outlook: Range of 4.18–4.35% with a neutral bias; budget progress would pull it toward 4.18%, while a government crisis or poor polls would lift it toward 4.35%.
fr5y.watch: Senate budget debate, presidential polls and euro-area PMIs.

fr10y.note: Down about 3–5bp to near 4.88%; spread to Bunds about 2bp tighter at near 153bp.
fr10y.why: OATs outperformed as haven buying during the US stock selloff spread to French debt and Le Pen's fiscal speech brought no new shock. That came despite the Commission seeing France with the euro area's weakest growth, 0.4% this year, a 5.5% deficit and debt rising to about 122% of GDP next year. The spread remains well below October's 177bp peak.
fr10y.outlook: Range of 4.80–4.98% with the spread at about 148–160bp; budget progress could tighten it toward 148bp, while a government crisis or weak polling would push it above 160bp.
fr10y.watch: Senate budget debate, presidential polls and the Dec 9 Senate vote.

fr30y.note: Down about 2bp to near 5.42%, still just below the US 30-year.
fr30y.why: Long OATs eased with the broader rally, though less than the 10-year because the Commission's forecasts of a deficit stuck above 5% and debt near 123% by 2028 keep long-dated buyers cautious. Political risk ahead of the 2027 presidential election still adds a premium.
fr30y.outlook: Range of 5.35–5.50% with a mild upward bias; a credible budget path could take it toward 5.35%, while a political setback or US 30-year yields above 5.55% would lift it toward 5.50%.
fr30y.watch: Senate budget debate, presidential polls and the US 20-year auction.

watch: Next: market reaction to Nvidia's beat, FOMC minutes, EIA stocks and euro-area final inflation Wed Nov 18; Dec WTI expiry, jobless claims and Anthropic's IPO Thu Nov 19; flash PMIs and the US 20-year auction this week; OPEC+ Nov 29, then the Fed Dec 8–9 and ECB Dec 17.
